title: Hardcoded credentials exposed in source code
reasoning: Multiple portal files contain hardcoded PIN codes stored as plain text constants in client-side code. These PINs are intended as access controls but are visible to anyone inspecting the JavaScript bundle. Client-side authentication provides zero security since the PIN values are shipped to the browser. An attacker can trivially bypass the PIN gate by reading the source or calling setUnlocked(true) directly.
reproduction: 1. Navigate to any portal page. 2. Open browser DevTools and search bundle for 'PIN'. 3. Read PIN value directly from source. 4. Alternatively, execute `setUnlocked(true)` in console to bypass entirely.
recommendation: Move authentication to the server. Implement proper session-based auth with bcrypt/scrypt hashed credentials stored server-side. Client should never see or validate credentials. The current PIN gate provides only visual obscurity, not security. If PINs must be used, validate them server-side via API call and issue a signed session token.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No test files are included in this feature. Client-side security vulnerabilities like exposed credentials are typically caught by security audits or static analysis, not unit tests.
minimumFixScope: All portal files (AnttipPortal.tsx, BasePortalDemo.tsx, BrianPortal.tsx, and any other portal files). Shared authentication service/API endpoint. Session management infrastructure.
